episodes.title: Morning Assessment Visit
episodes.text: You sit at the kitchen table with a new kid. You watch how they follow simple directions and handle small frustrations. You note what feels hard for them emotionally and mentally.

trial.title: What needs attention first
trial.scenario: You are assessing a kid to decide on next steps. They can stack blocks but shut down and cry when asked a simple question. They also fidget in the chair.
options: The shutdown and crying when asked to respond
The fidgeting in the chair
The way they stack blocks
trial.explain: The strong emotional reaction tells you most about what support to plan next.

episodes.title: Explaining Services At Home
episodes.text: You sit with a parent in their living room to go over services. They want to know what the agency can and cannot do.

choice.prompt: The parent looks confused about the requirements. What do you do?

options.label: Go over the services and requirements again slowly
options.outcome: You walk through each step again. They nod and write down what to bring next time.

options.label: Leave a simple summary and move on
options.outcome: You leave your notes on the table. They say they will read it later tonight.

chat.text: So what exactly do you do here?
What do we have to do to keep getting visits?
How often will you come to the house?

episodes.title: Writing The Care Plan
episodes.text: You sit down with your assessment notes. You match what you saw to small daily supports. You write out what to try and when.

episodes.title: Afternoon Group Time
episodes.text: You sit with the same group in the same room. You watch the same activity run the same way. You keep eyes on everyone until time is up.

episodes.title: When Group Gets Loud
episodes.text: You are watching the group when two kids start shouting over a game. The rest of the room stops and stares. You step in to use the behavior plan.

choice.prompt: Both kids are upset and the group is waiting. What do you do first?

options.label: Follow the calm-down steps in their care plans
options.outcome: You separate them and use the planned calming steps. The room settles enough to continue.

options.label: Pause the activity for the whole group
options.outcome: Everyone stops and sits quietly. You restart the game after a few minutes.

options.label: Let them work it out on their own
options.outcome: You stay close and watch. The shouting fades but the game does not continue smoothly.

episodes.title: Notes For Management
episodes.text: You sit at a desk and open your visit forms. You write down who you saw and what happened. You send the report to management before you leave.

episodes.title: Opening the Ledgers
episodes.text: You arrive at your desk and log in. You open the client's account books for the day. You check how transactions were recorded against accepted procedures.

episodes.title: Same Checks Again
episodes.text: You work through the same line-by-line checks as yesterday. You mark each entry for proper recording. Tomorrow you will do the same list again.

episodes.title: Setting Audit Scope
episodes.text: You sit down with the junior auditor to set today's scope. You review the list of branches together.

choice.prompt: You have limited hours today. How wide do you make the investigation?

options.label: Focus only on the north branch
options.outcome: You send the team to the north branch. You get a deep look there but leave the other sites for later.

options.label: Do a quick sweep of all three sites
options.outcome: You split the hours across all three sites. You see a little of each place but go less deep.

chat.text: We can't cover all three sites today. Which one needs us most?
The north branch had those control gaps last month.

episodes.title: Tracing Duplicate Payments
episodes.text: You pull last month's payment data into one sheet. You sort and compare entries to look for duplicated effort. You flag two matching payments to the same vendor.

trial.title: Spot what needs attention
trial.scenario: You review three payment lines. One follows policy, one has a missing approval, and one was paid twice for the same invoice.
options: The payment made twice for the same invoice
The payment that follows policy
The payment with correct approval
trial.explain: The duplicate payment points to deficient controls and needs attention first.

episodes.title: Finding a Gap
episodes.text: You compare receipts against policy and spot spending that breaks the rules. You pull the backup to confirm it is not a mistake. Your stomach tightens as the gap holds.

choice.prompt: You see possible non-compliance with management policy. What do you do right now?

options.label: Hold the finding and gather more proof first
options.outcome: You collect more records before raising it. You have stronger proof tomorrow but the issue sits one more day.

options.label: Flag it to your manager now
options.outcome: You alert your manager with what you have. The review starts today but you keep pulling proof after.

options.label: Ask the branch staff for explanation first
options.outcome: You ask staff what happened. You hear their side right away but they know you are looking.

episodes.title: Writing Up Findings
episodes.text: You sit down to prepare your detailed report on today's audit findings. You note how assets were used and where controls failed. You add your recommendations for changes in operations.

episodes.title: Morning Mortality Numbers
episodes.text: You arrive at your desk and open yesterday's statistical file. You sit down with the mortality and retirement figures and compare this month to last. You note where accident and sickness rates have shifted slightly.

episodes.title: Same Reserve Check
episodes.text: You open the same cash reserve sheet you check every morning. You compare the liabilities and benefit totals line by line. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Checking Pension Soundness
episodes.text: You sit down with a draft annuity plan waiting for review. You work through the premiums and test whether the funding holds for future payouts. You mark where the numbers still balance and where they do not.

episodes.title: Planning New Coverage
episodes.text: You join a call to plan an improvement to an existing line of business.

choice.prompt: The team waits for you to decide what to review first for the new plan idea.

options.label: Ask claims for recent sickness cases first
options.outcome: You get recent claim counts and use them to shape the first premium draft.

options.label: Ask programmers for the current pricing model first
options.outcome: You open the existing model together and see what would need to change.

chat.text: The underwriters want broader sickness coverage. Can we price it?
Programmers and claims are here too. What do you need from them first?

episodes.title: Reserve Shortfall Warning
episodes.text: You look again at the cash reserves against future benefits. The liabilities run higher than the reserves set aside. You know payouts must still be covered.

choice.prompt: You must decide how to handle the gap between reserves and future payouts.

options.label: Raise premium rates to cover the gap
options.outcome: You recalculate the required rates and send the higher figures for review.

options.label: Hold rates and raise reserves from other funds
options.outcome: You outline how much reserve must move over to meet future benefits.

options.label: Pause and recheck the liability estimates first
options.outcome: You rerun the disability and retirement estimates to confirm the gap is real.

episodes.title: Explaining Policy Choice
episodes.text: You sit down with company executives to explain a policy change. You walk them through what the premium and reserve numbers mean in plain terms. They ask what it means for policyholders.

trial.title: Answer in plain terms
trial.says: Can you explain why this policy costs what it does?
options: The rates reflect our mortality, sickness, and retirement estimates and the reserves needed for future benefits.
We set the price because that is how insurance has always been done.
You do not need to worry about the technical details.
trial.explain: The professional reply explains the technical basis in plain terms.

episodes.title: Opening the Front Desk
episodes.text: You arrive at the front desk and switch on the light. You sit down as the first visitors walk in. You greet each one and send them to the right person for their need.

episodes.title: Answering Morning Calls
episodes.text: You sit at the phone as calls start coming in. You answer and give a caller the office information they ask for. Another line starts blinking while you are still talking.

choice.prompt: The caller wants someone who is not at their desk. What do you do?

options.label: Take a message
options.outcome: You write down their name and number. The person calls them back later.

options.label: Transfer the call
options.outcome: You send the call through to voicemail. The caller leaves a message there.

options.label: Give office information
options.outcome: You answer what you can about hours and location. The caller says thanks and hangs up.

episodes.title: Typing Database Rows
episodes.text: You sit at your computer entering names into the database. You type one row after another from the same form. It is the same as yesterday and will be the same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Typing Up Notes
episodes.text: You sit down to type notes into a document on the computer. You work through the pages and fix small typos. You save the file when you finish.

trial.title: Order the document steps
items: Save the finished document
Open a blank document
Type the text from your notes
Read through to fix mistakes
trial.explain: You open, type, check, then save.

episodes.title: Phones and Visitor Line
episodes.text: You stand at the desk with a visitor waiting and two lines ringing at once. The phones keep ringing while the visitor looks at you.

choice.prompt: The phones are ringing and the visitor is waiting. What do you handle first?

options.label: Greet the visitor briefly
options.outcome: You tell them where to wait and who they will see. You pick up the ringing line.

options.label: Answer the phone first
options.outcome: You take the call and transfer it to your colleague. You turn back to the visitor.

chat.text: Hi, I need to see someone about my form?
Can you transfer line two to me please?
I can wait, but I am in a hurry.

episodes.title: Checking Payroll Hours
episodes.text: You sit down with the timekeeping sheet for payroll. You check the hours and enter them for processing. You submit the sheet for this pay period.

episodes.title: Morning System Check
episodes.text: You open your laptop and check the automation monitors. The status lights are green and match spec, same as yesterday. You log the numbers and close the tab.

episodes.title: Checking What Is Possible
episodes.text: You sit down with a user's request and read through what they need. You compare it against time and cost limits. You mark what fits and what does not.

episodes.title: Talking Through Limits
episodes.text: You join a call to talk design limits with the team.

choice.prompt: The team is waiting on your call about the design limit. What do you do?

options.label: Agree to the simpler design
options.outcome: You confirm the simpler design. The team updates the plan to match what the system can do.

options.label: Ask for one more check first
options.outcome: You ask for a quick check of the interface limits. The team pauses and brings back clearer numbers.

chat.text: The interface can't handle that extra step right now.
Can we simplify the design to fit performance?
If we cut that part, it will stay stable.

episodes.title: Writing the Test
episodes.text: You open the test doc for the automation update. You write each validation step in order. You get it ready for the team to run.

trial.title: Order the test steps
items: Run the check and record the result
Decide what the spec says to test
Fix and retest what fails
Write the steps to test it
trial.explain: You check the spec first, then write steps, run them, and fix what fails.

episodes.title: Install Stops Short
episodes.text: You are coordinating the software install when the system stops matching spec. The monitor shows an error and the install cannot finish. The team waits for your decision.

choice.prompt: The install is stuck and out of spec. What do you do first?

options.label: Pause the install and check the system
options.outcome: You pause the install. You check the monitor readings and find where it left spec.

options.label: Roll back to the last working version
options.outcome: You roll the system back. The old version runs again while you review the failed install.

options.label: Keep pushing the install through
options.outcome: You try to continue the install. The error stays and the system remains out of spec.

episodes.title: Writing It Down
episodes.text: You open the documentation for today's testing and install work. You note what was checked and what was installed. You save it where the team can find it.

episodes.title: Morning Wind Check
episodes.text: You sit down at the radar scope as the tower lights come on. You check wind speed, direction, and low visibility outside. You tell the first pilots what to expect before they move.

episodes.title: Clearing Morning Takeoffs
episodes.text: You watch two departures line up on different runways. You check the approach path is clear for an arrival. You pick up the mic to issue the next takeoff instruction.

choice.prompt: One departure is ready but an arrival is close on final. What do you do?

options.label: Hold the departure and clear the arrival to land first
options.outcome: You tell the departure to hold short. You clear the arrival to land and it touches down safely.

options.label: Clear the departure for immediate takeoff now
options.outcome: You clear the departure to go. You tell the arrival to go around and circle for another try.

episodes.title: Handing Flights Off
episodes.text: You pass each departing flight to the control center after takeoff. You accept each arriving flight back when they call in. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Watching Close Traffic
episodes.text: You notice two planes getting close on your screen. You call the pilot to point out the nearby traffic. You keep watching until they pass each other safely.

trial.title: Tell About Traffic
trial.says: Tower, this is flight 214, we are level at five thousand. Anything near us?
options: No reply, keep watching the screen quietly.
Flight 214, traffic at your two o'clock, same altitude, two miles.
Flight 214, just keep going, you will be fine.
trial.explain: You name where the nearby plane is so the pilot can see it.

episodes.title: Storm Emergency Call
episodes.text: You hear a pilot call in trouble in heavy rain and low visibility. You give a new flight path away from the worst weather. You stay with them and get ready to call for help.

choice.prompt: The pilot is losing visibility and needs a place to land. What do you do?

options.label: Give directions to the nearest emergency landing field
options.outcome: You read out headings to the emergency field. The pilot turns toward it and you alert emergency services to stand by.

options.label: Tell the pilot to hold course and wait out the storm
options.outcome: You give a safe holding path and updated weather. You keep talking to the pilot and alert emergency services to be ready.

episodes.title: Bringing Arrivals In
episodes.text: You take control of the evening arrivals from the center. You line them up and issue landing instructions one by one. You pass the last departure off before your shift ends.

episodes.title: Checking Nearby Rents
episodes.text: You arrive at your desk with coffee and open your listings. You pull up similar rentals nearby and compare nightly rates. You note which of your prices sit too high or too low.

episodes.title: Chasing Late Payment
episodes.text: You sit down to follow up on a late cleaning fee and deposit.

choice.prompt: The guest is confused about the extra charge. How do you handle it now?

options.label: Send the breakdown and payment link
options.outcome: You send the itemized fees and the link. He pays within the hour and thanks you for clarifying.

options.label: Offer a short extension to pay
options.outcome: You give him until tomorrow morning. He replies yes and you set a reminder to check again.

chat.text: Sorry, I thought that was already charged with the booking?
Can you send me the breakdown again?

episodes.title: Midday Systems Check
episodes.text: You log into each property dashboard like yesterday. You confirm locks, thermostats, and calendars look normal. Same checks tomorrow.

episodes.title: Planning Shower Repair
episodes.text: You walk the bathroom with a leaking shower. You list what the fix needs and what parts it will take. You line up the work around the next check-in.

trial.title: Order the repair steps
items: Schedule the work around bookings
Coordinate the contractor and guest access
Plan what the repair needs
Confirm the repair is complete
trial.explain: You plan first, then schedule, then coordinate, then confirm.

episodes.title: Burst Pipe Call
episodes.text: You get a call about water under the kitchen sink. You hurry over and see the supply line has split.

choice.prompt: Water is still spreading across the floor. What do you do first?

options.label: Shut off water and call emergency plumber
options.outcome: You stop the flow and the plumber arrives to replace the line. You mop up and move tonight's guest to another unit.

options.label: Wait for the regular handyman tomorrow
options.outcome: You put towels down and turn off the valve. The cabinet soaks overnight and needs extra drying work tomorrow.

episodes.title: Closing Monthly Numbers
episodes.text: You sit back down to close out the month. You enter rents collected and insurance, mortgage, and supply costs paid. You save the budget sheet and expense report for the owners.

episodes.title: Morning Run Schedule
episodes.text: You arrive early and sit down with yesterday's notes. You build today's daily work and run schedule. You match crews and service vehicles to the requests on hand.

episodes.title: Watching The Radio
episodes.text: You sit by the radio and telephone for your assigned territory. You listen and answer short checks. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Customer Calls With Changes
episodes.text: You take a call from a customer who needs service at a different location. You talk through what they need and what you have free. You check the schedule with your supervisor.

choice.prompt: The customer wants a different location than planned. What do you do?

options.label: Move a crew to the new location
options.outcome: You update the schedule and dispatch the crew to the new location. The customer confirms the change.

options.label: Keep the original schedule
options.outcome: You explain you are keeping the original plan for today. The customer agrees to wait for the next run.

episodes.title: Sending Crews Out
episodes.text: You look at the customer requests and specifications. You pick the right work crew and equipment for each location. You send them out by radio and telephone.

trial.title: Dispatch in order
items: Call the crew on the radio or telephone
Read the customer request and specifications
Send the crew and equipment to the location
Pick the crew and equipment to send
trial.explain: You read the request first, then pick the crew, then send them.

episodes.title: Crew Problem Call
episodes.text: A field crew calls in with a problem at their location.

choice.prompt: The crew is waiting for help. What do you send first?

options.label: Relay a new work order by radio
options.outcome: You relay the updated work order right away. The crew starts work with the new instructions.

options.label: Tell them to wait while you check
options.outcome: You ask them to stand by while you confer with the supervisor. You call back once you have an answer.

options.label: Send a different service vehicle
options.outcome: You dispatch another service vehicle with the right equipment. The crew waits until it arrives.

chat.text: We are at the location but need different equipment.
What do they need to finish the work order?
Can you relay a new work order to us?

episodes.title: Passing Along Messages
episodes.text: You sit back at the desk and pick up the telephone. You relay work orders and messages between crews and supervisors. You keep the information moving across your territory.

episodes.title: Morning Inspection Walk
episodes.text: You arrive on the hangar floor and pull on your gloves. You start your routine inspection on the parked aircraft. You move panel by panel and check off each item as required.

episodes.title: Landing Gear Check
episodes.text: You kneel under the wing and look over the landing gear. You check the hydraulic lines and deicer boots for cracks, breaks, and leaks. You run your light slowly along each fitting.

trial.title: Find the problem first
trial.scenario: You are examining the landing gear, hydraulic lines, and deicer boot. The gear looks solid, one hydraulic fitting is wet with fluid, and the boot has light dust on it.
options: Wipe dust off the deicer boot
Look closer at the wet hydraulic fitting for a leak
Move on to the next aircraft
trial.explain: A wet fitting points to an active hydraulic leak that needs attention first.

episodes.title: Manuals on the Bench
episodes.text: You sit down with the maintenance manual and the service bulletin. You read the specs for the worn component you found. You compare the repair method against the replacement method.

choice.prompt: The manual allows a repair but the bulletin leans toward replacement. What do you do?

options.label: Follow the replacement steps in the bulletin
options.outcome: You pull the replacement procedure and order the part before you touch the aircraft.

options.label: Recheck the manual limits and measurements first
options.outcome: You remeasure the wear and confirm whether it still falls inside repairable limits.

episodes.title: Afternoon Repeat Checks
episodes.text: You do the same scheduled checks you did this morning. You look at the same panels and the same gauges. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Leak on the Line
episodes.text: You spot fresh fluid under a hydraulic line during a special inspection. Your lead walks over to look with you.

choice.prompt: Fluid is still seeping from the fitting. What do you do?

options.label: Ground it and keep inspecting the leak
options.outcome: You keep the aircraft parked and trace the leak source before anyone clears it.

options.label: Wipe it and watch it for a few minutes
options.outcome: You clean the area and watch to see how fast fluid comes back.

options.label: Call for the manual limits right away
options.outcome: You pull up the specs to check if this leak is outside allowed limits.

chat.text: That line was dry this morning. How bad is it?
We have a departure waiting. Can it stay or does it ground?

episodes.title: Logs and Sign Off
episodes.text: You sit at the desk and open the repair logs. You write down all the preventive and corrective work from today. You inspect the finished job once more and certify the aircraft is ready.

episodes.title: The core work
episodes.text: You start the main work of a Amazon FBA Seller — the core of the job, done properly, start to finish. No audience and no shortcut: this is the thing everything else in the day supports. This is the work the whole job is built around.

episodes.title: People time
episodes.text: People need things from you — questions, help, decisions. You deal with them one at a time, the way this job always does. Real people, real reactions — this is the human side of the job, as it actually feels.

choice.prompt: Someone you're working with asks you to take on one more thing — extra work, on top of everything already in front of you today.

options.label: Say yes and fit it in
options.outcome: You fit it in. The day runs longer, the work gets done properly — and the person who asked remembers that you said yes.

options.label: Say no, politely
options.outcome: You say no, and you say why. A short, slightly awkward moment — then the rest of your day stays yours.

options.label: Offer a smaller version
options.outcome: You offer the part you can actually do, and by when. Most days that's accepted — saying yes to everything is how this job burns people out.

episodes.title: Hands on
episodes.text: Tools-and-systems time: you work the equipment and the screens of the trade until the thing in front of you does what it should. Skilled, hands-on work — the part where being good at it shows.

trial.title: The check-in
trial.says: Hey — how's that thing coming along that you were working on?
options: It's on track. I'll flag it straight away if I need help or it slips.
Fine.
Honestly? Don't ask. It's a disaster.
trial.explain: The professional reply says where things stand and what happens next — short, honest, no drama.

episodes.title: The routine block
episodes.text: The same block as yesterday: the repeating tasks that never make the brochure. You do them again, carefully, because skipping them is exactly how mistakes happen. The same again tomorrow. This block repeats more than any other part of the job.

episodes.title: It goes wrong
episodes.text: Something goes wrong — it always does, some days. A problem lands on you that was in nobody's plan, and sorting it out is now your job. Unplanned and unavoidable — how the job feels when it pushes back.

episodes.title: The paperwork
episodes.text: End of day: notes, records, the write-up of everything you did. The work isn't finished until it's written down. Nobody's favourite part. It still has to be done, every day.

episodes.title: Morning Label Sketches
episodes.text: You sit down and open yesterday's product carton sketches. You draw clean basic illustrations for the front label. You adjust the lines until they read clearly at small size.

episodes.title: Campaign Check In
episodes.text: You join the multimedia campaign table to coordinate today's production work.

choice.prompt: The team needs help with background design but the schedule is already full. What do you do?

options.label: Take the two shots now
options.outcome: You take them and stay late to finish your own shots. The schedule slips by an hour.

options.label: Offer one shot today
options.outcome: You take one shot and note the second for tomorrow. The board stays current.

options.label: Stay on your own shots
options.outcome: You keep your plan and flag the gap. A colleague reassigns the extra work.

chat.text: We are behind on background design. Can you take two shots?
Check the schedule first. Tell us what fits today.

episodes.title: Building Complex Motion
episodes.text: You open your computer and build a complex graphic sequence. You shape the movement frame by frame with your own judgment. You play it back and fix the rough timing.

episodes.title: File Version Check
episodes.text: You open the configuration control system. You check file names and save the current versions. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Deadline Sequence Crunch
episodes.text: You script and plan a short animated narrative sequence due by end of day. You switch between hand drawing and computer software to get it done. The clock keeps moving while you work.

choice.prompt: The storyboards are rough and the deadline is tight. How do you finish the sequence?

options.label: Lock the script and animate
options.outcome: You lock the simple script and finish the shots. The sequence is plain but complete on time.

options.label: Keep revising the story
options.outcome: You keep changing the plan and run out of time. Two shots stay unfinished.

episodes.title: Budget and Progress Log
episodes.text: You sit with the campaign budget and schedule. You log today's background design work. You mark progress against the plan.

trial.title: Order the campaign steps
items: Track progress and update the schedule
Create background designs
Handle budgeting and scheduling
Coordinate production work
trial.explain: Budget and schedule come first, then coordination, design, and tracking.

episodes.title: First Call Morning
episodes.text: You arrive at the house and knock on the door. You greet the customer and ask what the fridge is doing wrong. You glance at the work order to check what was reported.

choice.prompt: The customer describes a noise and the work order says something different. Which do you follow up first?

options.label: Ask about the noise first
options.outcome: You ask when the noise happens and the customer shows you. You write that down with the work order note.

options.label: Go by the work order first
options.outcome: You read the work order back to the customer and ask if that is still happening. You note what they confirm.

episodes.title: Watching The Washer
episodes.text: You stand by the washer and start a cycle. You watch and listen as it runs. You look for loose parts and signs of leaking fluid.

episodes.title: Water On Floor
episodes.text: You see water spreading under the dishwasher while it runs.

choice.prompt: Water is leaking while the dishwasher is running. What do you do right now?

options.label: Stop the machine and check the leak
options.outcome: You stop the cycle and look at where the fluid is coming from. You keep watching for loose parts around the leak.

options.label: Let it run a little longer to watch
options.outcome: You stay with the machine and watch the leak closely for a short moment. You then stop it to avoid more water on the floor.

chat.text: Is that water supposed to be coming out?
Should I turn it off?

episodes.title: Manual Pages Again
episodes.text: You sit in the van and open the troubleshooting guide. You check the same kind of chart you checked yesterday. You turn the pages and find the section you need again.

episodes.title: Tracing The Circuit
episodes.text: You open the schematic drawing for the dryer. You trace the electrical circuit following the diagram. You test with the circuit tester to locate the short and ground.

trial.title: Put the circuit check in order
items: Test the circuit with the circuit tester
Locate the short or ground
Open the schematic drawing
Trace the circuit following the diagram
trial.explain: You look at the drawing first, then trace, test, and find the fault.

episodes.title: Bill At Door
episodes.text: You add up the repair work at the kitchen table. You hand the bill to the customer and explain the charges. You collect the payment before you leave.

episodes.title: Cleaning Your Tools
episodes.text: You arrive at the yard and lay your saws and clippers on the bench. You wipe off yesterday's sap and check each edge before the truck leaves.

trial.title: Get tools ready
items: Lubricate the joints and moving parts
Sharpen the cutting edge
Wipe the sap and dirt clean
Check that the tool moves right
trial.explain: You clean first so you can see the edge, then sharpen and oil it.

episodes.title: Setting Up Trucks
episodes.text: You drive the truck to the street and park the boom truck under the oak. You unload the power saws, ropes, and block and tackle.

episodes.title: Hoisting Tools Up
episodes.text: You stand below as your climber settles into the crown. You clip tools to the rope for him.

choice.prompt: He is waiting on the rope. What do you send up first?

options.label: Send the handsaw first
options.outcome: He cuts the dead limb he is tied in next to, then asks for the shears.

options.label: Send the shears first
options.outcome: He trims small twigs while the big dead limb stays in his way.

chat.text: Send up the handsaw first, please.
Then I need the shears for the small stuff.

episodes.title: Feeding the Chipper
episodes.text: You stand at the brush chipper and feed in limbs and brush. You push one armload in, then the next. It is the same as yesterday, and the same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Branch Over Wires
episodes.text: You are clearing branches around the power lines from the bucket. A cut limb hangs up on the wire and will not drop. You hold the rope that lowers it.

choice.prompt: The limb is resting on the line. What do you do?

options.label: Hold tension and wait for the spotter
options.outcome: You keep the rope tight while he checks the line. You lower the limb clear on his signal.

options.label: Pull hard to free it now
options.outcome: The limb swings and bounces on the wire. You have to stop and reset the rope.

options.label: Cut another branch to lighten it
options.outcome: You make a second small cut with the saw. The limb lifts off and you lower it down.

episodes.title: Lowering the Last Limbs
episodes.text: You tie off the last cut branches with rope and block and tackle. You call clear and lower them slow to the ground. You feed the brush into the chipper to finish the pile.

episodes.title: Morning Team Huddle
episodes.text: You arrive and sit down with the creative, art, and copy leads. You walk through what the client asked for and what you could show. You agree who handles each part of the work.

episodes.title: Client Goals Call
episodes.text: You sit down with the client to talk through goals and limits. You ask what they need and what they can spend.

choice.prompt: The client wants two style directions but the budget is tight. What do you do?

options.label: Offer two small directions that fit the budget
options.outcome: You explain what each small direction covers. The client picks one to move forward with.

options.label: Offer one direction only to stay in budget
options.outcome: You show what one direction can cover for the money. The client agrees to start there.

chat.text: We need it simple and clear for new customers.
Our budget is tight this time.
Can you still show us two style directions?

episodes.title: Working Through Layouts
episodes.text: You sit beside the creative director with early layouts between you. You talk through what works and what feels off. You adjust the design solution together piece by piece.

trial.title: Answering design feedback
trial.says: This layout feels crowded — what should we change?
options: We can simplify the layout and give the main message more room.
The client will probably approve it anyway, let's leave it.
Good taste is hard to explain, we'll know it when we see it.
trial.explain: The professional reply stays focused on improving the design solution.

episodes.title: Budget and Schedule Check
episodes.text: You sit with your project list and check budget and dates. You move the same numbers forward another day. It looks the same as yesterday and will look the same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Layout Approval Stall
episodes.text: You lay out the final designs for the client to approve. The client pauses and does not want to sign off yet. You sit with the work in front of you waiting for a call.

choice.prompt: The client will not approve the final layouts right now. What do you do?

options.label: Ask what needs to change for approval
options.outcome: You listen and write down each concern. You leave with clear fixes to bring back.

options.label: Ask for more time and set a new review
options.outcome: The client agrees to a second look next week. You keep the layouts as they are for now.

options.label: Walk through the layouts again slowly
options.outcome: You explain each choice against what they asked for. The client points to the part that still bothers them.

episodes.title: Project Notes Update
episodes.text: You sit back at your desk and update your account notes. You write down costs so far and what is due next. You file the project where you can find it tomorrow.

episodes.title: Morning Ankle Check
episodes.text: You arrive before practice and set out your kit by the bench. A runner limps in holding a swollen ankle from yesterday. You ask what happened, look at the joint, and check if she can bear weight to decide about a doctor visit.

episodes.title: Ice and Compression Line
episodes.text: You sit with the same three athletes as yesterday for their morning care. You wrap ice, check the time, and swap wraps. Same chairs, same timers, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Update for Coach
episodes.text: You meet the head coach on the sideline to report on two recovering players.

choice.prompt: The coach wants both players full tomorrow, but one is still limping. What do you report?

options.label: Report both as they are
options.outcome: You tell him one is improving and one is still limited. He adjusts tomorrow's plan around that.

options.label: Hold the limping player back
options.outcome: You tell him the limping player is not ready for full work. She stays on limited drills another day.

chat.text: How are my two wingers doing today?
Can I have them full for tomorrow?

episodes.title: Heat and Rehab Work
episodes.text: You bring a sore shoulder back into the training room after lunch. You position him on the table and start the set care with heat and guided movement. You watch how he responds and ease off when it pulls.

trial.title: Order the injury care
items: Apply the planned therapy care to the injured area
Check the injury and confirm the care plan
Track how the athlete responds during the care
Get the athlete settled and positioned for treatment
trial.explain: You check first, then position, then treat, then watch the response.

episodes.title: Knee Twist on Field
episodes.text: You run out when a player goes down holding her knee.

choice.prompt: The knee is swelling fast and she cannot bear weight. What do you do now?

options.label: Give on-field care and refer out
options.outcome: You steady the knee, give first care, and send her to the physician today for a full diagnosis.

options.label: Keep her with you for now
options.outcome: You help her off, keep weight off the knee, and watch her closely before deciding on referral.

options.label: Let her try to walk it off
options.outcome: You keep her seated and recheck the knee. She stays off it until you finish the assessment.

chat.text: It popped when I turned. I can't stand on it.
Do you need us to call the doctor?

episodes.title: Notes and Reports Done
episodes.text: You sit down at the desk after practice. You write up today's assessments, care, and clearances. You file the reports so the record matches what happened.

episodes.title: The core work
episodes.text: You start the main work of a Audio-Video Equipment Technician — the core of the job, done properly, start to finish. No audience and no shortcut: this is the thing everything else in the day supports. This is the work the whole job is built around.

episodes.title: People time
episodes.text: People need things from you — questions, help, decisions. You deal with them one at a time, the way this job always does. Real people, real reactions — this is the human side of the job, as it actually feels.

choice.prompt: Someone you're working with asks you to take on one more thing — extra work, on top of everything already in front of you today.

options.label: Say yes and fit it in
options.outcome: You fit it in. The day runs longer, the work gets done properly — and the person who asked remembers that you said yes.

options.label: Say no, politely
options.outcome: You say no, and you say why. A short, slightly awkward moment — then the rest of your day stays yours.

options.label: Offer a smaller version
options.outcome: You offer the part you can actually do, and by when. Most days that's accepted — saying yes to everything is how this job burns people out.

episodes.title: Hands on
episodes.text: Hands-on time. You make, fix or adjust the real thing in front of you — the part of the job you can touch, and the part where skill is visible. Skilled, hands-on work — the part where being good at it shows.

trial.title: The check-in
trial.says: Hey — how's that thing coming along that you were working on?
options: It's on track. I'll flag it straight away if I need help or it slips.
Fine.
Honestly? Don't ask. It's a disaster.
trial.explain: The professional reply says where things stand and what happens next — short, honest, no drama.

episodes.title: The routine block
episodes.text: The same block as yesterday: the repeating tasks that never make the brochure. You do them again, carefully, because skipping them is exactly how mistakes happen. The same again tomorrow. This block repeats more than any other part of the job.

episodes.title: It goes wrong
episodes.text: Something goes wrong — it always does, some days. A problem lands on you that was in nobody's plan, and sorting it out is now your job. Unplanned and unavoidable — how the job feels when it pushes back.

episodes.title: The paperwork
episodes.text: End of day: notes, records, the write-up of everything you did. The work isn't finished until it's written down. Nobody's favourite part. It still has to be done, every day.

episodes.title: Morning Hearing Test
episodes.text: You arrive and bring your first patient back to the quiet test room. You place the headphones and check the tones on your equipment. You watch and mark each response as you go.

trial.title: Run the hearing test
items: Mark down the type and degree of loss
Seat the patient and place the headphones
Check the test equipment is working
Present tones and watch for responses
trial.explain: You set up the patient and equipment first, test, then record what you found.

episodes.title: Explaining the Results
episodes.text: You sit down with the patient to go over what the test showed.

choice.prompt: The test points to hearing loss and you need to name the next step. What do you suggest now?

options.label: Lay out the likely diagnosis and treatment path
options.outcome: You explain the findings plainly and write down the treatment options to consider next.

options.label: Suggest waiting and retesting next month
options.outcome: You book a follow-up test and note why you held off on treatment for now.

chat.text: So is this just getting older, or something else?
What do we actually do about it?

episodes.title: Fitting New Aids
episodes.text: You sit with a patient to fit their new hearing aids. You place each aid, adjust the fit, and test the sound. You show them how to put them in and take them out.

episodes.title: Same Checks Again
episodes.text: You run the midday rechecks on stable patients. You ask the same questions, check hearing status, and note small changes. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Aid Stopped Working
episodes.text: A patient comes in upset because one hearing aid has gone dead. You look it over at the desk and see wax blocking the sound path. It needs cleaning and a quick repair before they leave.

choice.prompt: The patient needs to hear tonight and your afternoon is full. What do you do?

options.label: Clean and repair it now at the bench
options.outcome: You clear the blockage, test the aid, and hand it back working before the next appointment.

options.label: Lend a spare and repair it later
options.outcome: You fit a loaner aid for tonight and set the broken one aside for repair after hours.

options.label: Send it out for repair
options.outcome: You pack up the aid and explain the wait while the patient manages with one ear.

episodes.title: Writing Up Notes
episodes.text: You sit at the desk and open today's patient records. You log each test, fitting, and follow-up check. You save and close each chart when it is complete.

episodes.title: Drive to First House
episodes.text: You load your buckets, hose, and vacuum into the van. You drive across town to the customer's home. You park out front and get your gear ready.

episodes.title: Hello at the Door
episodes.text: You walk up as the customer comes out with the keys. You talk through where to wash the car.

choice.prompt: Where do you set up to wash the car?

options.label: Pull into the driveway
options.outcome: You drive the car into the driveway. You have flat space and the hose reaches easily.

options.label: Stay parked on the street
options.outcome: You leave everything on the street. You carry buckets back and forth and keep clear of traffic.

chat.text: Morning! Driveway is free if you want to pull in.
Actually you're the boss today. You pick the spot.
Just let me know if you need the hose spigot.

episodes.title: Scrubbing Floor Mats
episodes.text: You pull the floor mats out. You scrub them with brush and cleaner. You rinse them again. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Waxing the Hood
episodes.text: You lay masking around the trim. You rub wax into the hood in slow circles. You let it haze and buff it clean.

episodes.title: Bugs Stuck Fast
episodes.text: You scrub the front bumper and grill. The dried insects do not move. You stand back and look at the stuck mess.

choice.prompt: The bugs are baked on. What do you do?

options.label: Soak again and use soft brush
options.outcome: You spray cleaner on and wait. The bugs soften and brush off without marking the paint.

options.label: Scrape hard to get it done
options.outcome: You scrape hard at the spots. The bugs come off but you leave fine scratches in the clear coat.

options.label: Leave it and move on
options.outcome: You rinse and leave the spots there. The bumper looks clean except for the dark specks up close.

episodes.title: Rinse and Dry
episodes.text: You rinse the mats and the outside of the car clean. You shake the water off. You finish drying with cloth and air.

trial.title: Dry the mats right
items: Wipe leftover water with a cloth
Rinse the mats clean with the hose
Blow the seams dry with air
Set the mats on the drying rack
trial.explain: You rinse first, then rack, then cloth, then air for the last water.

episodes.title: Morning Work Orders
episodes.text: You arrive and hang up your jacket. You sit down at the bench and pull up today's work orders. You read through each one to see what needs inspecting and fixing.

episodes.title: Checking for Damage
episodes.text: You walk around the first car with your clipboard. You look close for dents, leaks, and worn parts. You write down everything you find so repairs can be planned.

choice.prompt: You see a small crack you are not sure about. Do you write it down now?

options.label: Write it down now
options.outcome: You note the crack on the form. The supervisor sees it and adds it to the repair list.

options.label: Leave it off for now
options.outcome: You skip it on the form. It stays unlisted until the next inspection catches it.

episodes.title: Test Drive and Testing
episodes.text: You take the car out for a short test drive. You come back and hook up the compression gauge and diagnostic device. You watch the readings to check the engine and systems.

trial.title: What needs attention
trial.scenario: You test drive the car and then test the systems. The steering feels normal. The diagnostic device shows one system reading far outside its normal range.
options: The system with the bad reading
The steering that feels normal
The clean windshield
trial.explain: You check the system that tests outside its normal range first.

episodes.title: Brakes Again
episodes.text: You sit at the lift and work through another set of brakes. You reline and adjust them the same way as yesterday. Same tools, same steps, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Brake Test Fails
episodes.text: You test the repaired brakes you just adjusted. The pedal still feels low and will not meet spec. You have to decide what to do next.

choice.prompt: The repaired brakes still do not meet spec. What do you do?

options.label: Keep adjusting and retest
options.outcome: You adjust the brakes again and run the test once more. The reading tells you if it now meets spec.

options.label: Stop and recheck the repair
options.outcome: You pull the wheel and look over the repair. You find what is off before you test again.

episodes.title: Talk With Supervisor
episodes.text: You walk over to your supervisor with your notes. You go over what you tested and fixed today.

chat.text: What did you find on the morning car?
Did the brakes meet spec after the retest?
Okay, leave the work order with me.

episodes.title: The core work
episodes.text: You start the main work of a Avionics Technician — the core of the job, done properly, start to finish. No audience and no shortcut: this is the thing everything else in the day supports. This is the work the whole job is built around.

episodes.title: People time
episodes.text: A quiet stretch: mostly you and the work. Human contact in this job is the exception, not the rule — long solo runs are the normal texture of the day. Real people, real reactions — this is the human side of the job, as it actually feels.

choice.prompt: A message lands: could you also take on one more thing today — extra work, on top of everything already in front of you?

options.label: Say yes and fit it in
options.outcome: You fit it in. The day runs longer, the work gets done properly — and the person who asked remembers that you said yes.

options.label: Say no, politely
options.outcome: You say no, and you say why. A short, slightly awkward moment — then the rest of your day stays yours.

options.label: Offer a smaller version
options.outcome: You offer the part you can actually do, and by when. Most days that's accepted — saying yes to everything is how this job burns people out.

episodes.title: Hands on
episodes.text: Hands-on time. You make, fix or adjust the real thing in front of you — the part of the job you can touch, and the part where skill is visible. Skilled, hands-on work — the part where being good at it shows.

trial.title: The check-in
trial.says: Hey — how's that thing coming along that you were working on?
options: It's on track. I'll flag it straight away if I need help or it slips.
Fine.
Honestly? Don't ask. It's a disaster.
trial.explain: The professional reply says where things stand and what happens next — short, honest, no drama.

episodes.title: The routine block
episodes.text: The same block as yesterday: the repeating tasks that never make the brochure. You do them again, carefully, because skipping them is exactly how mistakes happen. The same again tomorrow. This block repeats more than any other part of the job.

episodes.title: It goes wrong
episodes.text: Something goes wrong — it always does, some days. A problem lands on you that was in nobody's plan, and sorting it out is now your job. Unplanned and unavoidable — how the job feels when it pushes back.

episodes.title: The paperwork
episodes.text: End of day: notes, records, the write-up of everything you did. The work isn't finished until it's written down. Nobody's favourite part. It still has to be done, every day.

episodes.title: Shelf Space Talk
episodes.text: You arrive at the first store and walk the aisle with the manager. Your top shelf spots are gone and your boxes sit low. You ask for better exposure for the week.

choice.prompt: The manager says you can have the end spot if you pay for the extra ad sign. What do you do?

options.label: Take the end spot with the sign
options.outcome: You agree to the sign and move your products to the end spot where shoppers pass.

options.label: Keep your current shelf for now
options.outcome: You stay on the low shelf and tell the manager you will check sales again next visit.

episodes.title: Questions at the Counter
episodes.text: You sit down in the back office while the shop owner flips through your list.

chat.text: How much is this case, and when can you deliver?
Can customers pay on credit for this line?

episodes.title: Counting the Same Shelves
episodes.text: You walk the same three aisles with your notebook. You count cans and boxes, mark what is low, and write the same reorder. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Building the Display
episodes.text: You kneel on the store floor and build the small promo display. You plan the layout, snap the stand together, and fill it row by row. You step back to check it looks full and straight.

trial.title: Build the Display
items: Stock products onto the shelves
Plan where the display will sit
Assemble the display stand
Check the floor space you have
trial.explain: You check the space, plan the layout, build the stand, then stock it.

episodes.title: Display Pushed Aside
episodes.text: You arrive at the second store for the promo start. Your display is pushed into the back corner and another brand is in your spot. The clerk says there was no room this morning.

choice.prompt: The promo starts in an hour and your products are in the back. What do you do?

options.label: Ask to rebuild the display up front
options.outcome: You move the small stand back near the register and restock it before shoppers come in.

options.label: Leave it in back and adjust the plan
options.outcome: You leave the stand where it is and suggest a smaller counter display for the front instead.

options.label: Call the manager to discuss placement
options.outcome: You find the manager and review the agreed shelf and ad spot for this week.

episodes.title: Suggesting What Fits
episodes.text: You sit with the last shopkeeper and look at what sold last month. You point to two products that match her regular buyers. You explain how each one fits her shelf and her customers.

episodes.title: First Mix
episodes.text: You arrive in the cool bakery. You set your bag down and tie your apron. You measure flour and sugar and tip them into the big mixing bowl.

trial.title: Mix in order
items: Start the mixer to blend the ingredients
Place measured flour and sugar in the mixing bowl
Check the dough looks mixed as instructed
Set the time and speed controls on the mixer
trial.explain: You place ingredients first, then set controls before you start mixing.

episodes.title: Setting Ovens
episodes.text: You walk to the production ovens. You turn the dial to the temperature on the sheet. You lift the tray and place it into the hot oven.

choice.prompt: The oven is still heating and not at temperature yet. Do you load the tray now?

options.label: Wait for temperature
options.outcome: You wait a few minutes. The light shows ready and you slide the tray in.

options.label: Load it now
options.outcome: You slide the tray in early. The bake starts slow and you watch it closely.

episodes.title: Pans Again
episodes.text: You sit at the bench with sheets of dough. You place dough in pans, one after another. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Shaping Dough
episodes.text: You dust the bench with flour. You press the dough into molds and smooth the tops. You set the filled pans in a row for the oven.

episodes.title: Bad Batch
episodes.text: You pull a tray and stop to check products for quality. You see dark burnt bottoms.

choice.prompt: You find several burnt and damaged rolls. What do you do with them?

options.label: Set damaged ones aside
options.outcome: You pull the burnt rolls off the tray. The good ones stay for packing.

options.label: Leave them with the rest
options.outcome: You leave them on the tray. They move down the line with the good rolls.

chat.text: How do those look?
Pull any damaged ones aside.

episodes.title: Morning Bake
episodes.text: You lay the last dough on sheets. You carry them to the production ovens. You bake them and watch them rise and brown.

episodes.title: Morning Cash Count
episodes.text: You arrive before anyone else and unlock the office. You count yesterday's cash and sort the bills for the bank. You seal the deposit bag and lock it in your bag.

episodes.title: Setting The Standard
episodes.text: You sit down with the morning staff before opening. You tell them what good service looks like today. You watch them nod and take their stations.

choice.prompt: One server is late again and looks distracted. What do you do before you open?

options.label: Remind the whole team of the standard
options.outcome: You restate the start-time rule for everyone. The late server apologizes and gets to work.

options.label: Speak to the late server privately
options.outcome: You pull them aside and set a clear expectation. They nod and start their side work.

episodes.title: Welcome In
episodes.text: You stand by the front door as guests come in.

trial.title: Seat new guests
items: Walk them to their table
Greet them at the door
Hand them the wine list
Hand them the menu
trial.explain: You greet first, then seat them, then give the menu and wine list.

chat.text: Hi, table for two please?
Can we see the menus?
Do you have a wine list too?

episodes.title: Watching The Room
episodes.text: You stand near the counter and watch the room. Same tables, same pours, same checking of IDs as yesterday. You stay in place and keep watching until the rush thins.

episodes.title: Checking The Pour
episodes.text: You see a regular order a second glass for a young friend.

choice.prompt: The young guest has no ID to show. What do you do?

options.label: Stop the pour and step in
options.outcome: You tell the table you cannot serve without ID. The regular pays for his own glass and the moment passes.

options.label: Watch closely and check ID yourself
options.outcome: You walk over and ask for ID directly. When there is none, you refuse the second pour.

chat.text: He says it's fine, he's with her.
Should I still pour it?

episodes.title: Sanitation Logbook
episodes.text: You sit down with the sanitation binder in the back. You copy today's cleaning times and temperatures into the form. You file it for the health inspector to see.

episodes.title: Tools Ready First
episodes.text: You arrive and flip on the lights. You clean and sterilize your scissors, combs, and clippers before anyone sits down.

trial.title: Check the tray
trial.scenario: You lay out your scissors, combs, and clippers. The scissors look clean, one comb is clean, but the clippers still have hair stuck between the blades.
options: The clippers still have hair and need cleaning again
The scissors are ready to cut hair
The clean comb is ready to use
trial.explain: The clippers are the only tool that is still dirty.

episodes.title: First Chair Talk
episodes.text: A man sits down and you turn him toward the mirror.

choice.prompt: He is vague and you need a clear style before you cut. What do you do?

options.label: Ask about length on top and sides
options.outcome: He points to show an inch off the top and tighter sides. You now know what to cut.

options.label: Start cutting and guess the style
options.outcome: You start trimming and he keeps shifting, unsure if you understood him.

chat.text: Just clean it up, you know?
Keep the top, but shorter on the sides I guess.
Like last time, sort of.

episodes.title: Midmorning Cut
episodes.text: You drape the cloth around the next customer's shoulders and pin it snug. You ask what she wants, then you cut and trim with clippers, comb, and scissors. You check the sides in the mirror and even them up.

episodes.title: Sweeping Between Clients
episodes.text: You brush hair off the chair and wipe the station. You sweep the floor around your chair. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Uneven Side Fix
episodes.text: You finish a cut and the left side looks longer than the right. The customer sees it too and goes quiet.

choice.prompt: You have clippers and scissors in hand and he is waiting. What do you do?

options.label: Stop and ask what he sees
options.outcome: He points to the longer side. You recomb it and trim it even.

options.label: Tell him it looks fine and remove the cloth
options.outcome: He pays but keeps checking the side in the mirror by the door.

options.label: Recomb both sides and blend them even
options.outcome: You trim carefully and the sides match. He nods when you show him.

episodes.title: Last Chair Cleanup
episodes.text: You take off the cloth and shake it out. You sweep the floor and wipe your station. You rinse the combs and wipe down the scissors and clippers.

episodes.title: First Regular Order
episodes.text: You clock in behind the counter and open the register. A regular steps up and you take her order for a hot coffee. You call it back to your coworker on bar to start it.

episodes.title: Explaining the Menu
episodes.text: A new customer stares up at the board and looks stuck. You describe the espresso drinks and the brewed coffees in plain terms. You suggest the blended coffee because she says she likes things cold and sweet.

choice.prompt: She asks if she should get the large blended coffee or just try a small tea first. What do you do?

options.label: Suggest the small tea to start
options.outcome: She orders the small tea and thanks you for not pushing the bigger drink.

options.label: Suggest the large blended coffee
options.outcome: She orders the large blended coffee and you ring it up and pass the order on.

episodes.title: Making Morning Lattes
episodes.text: You stay on bar through the morning rush. You pull shots and steam milk for one latte after another. You set each finished drink on the pickup counter.

trial.title: Line up the latte steps
items: Pour the shots and milk together
Pull the espresso shots
Hand the cup to the customer
Steam the milk
trial.explain: You pull shots, steam milk, pour them together, then hand it off.

episodes.title: Wiping Down Again
episodes.text: The rush passes and you wipe down the counters and rinse the utensils. You sanitize the same work areas you did yesterday. Tomorrow you will do it again.

episodes.title: Card Reader Fails
episodes.text: The lunch line is long and the card reader stops working.

choice.prompt: The customer has no cash and three people are waiting behind. What do you do?

options.label: Ask them to step aside while you take cash orders
options.outcome: They step aside and you keep taking cash payments while the reader restarts.

options.label: Take their order and hold it until the reader works
options.outcome: You write down their drink order and tell them you will run payment once it is back.

chat.text: My card just got declined. Is it my card?
Reader is down. Take cash or have them wait.

episodes.title: Afternoon Till Rush
episodes.text: You work the register through the afternoon pickup. You receive each payment and count back change for cash. You hand out receipts and call the next order.

episodes.title: Cleaning Stations Again
episodes.text: You arrive early and wipe down the work stations. You wash the combs and sanitize the scissors. It is the same as yesterday, and the same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Morning Booking Calls
episodes.text: You sit down with the appointment book open. A customer wants a slot today.

choice.prompt: You have one late morning slot and one mid-afternoon slot open. Which do you offer her?

options.label: Offer the late morning slot
options.outcome: You write her name in the late morning slot. The afternoon stays open for someone else.

options.label: Offer the mid-afternoon slot
options.outcome: You write her name in the mid-afternoon slot. The late morning stays open for someone else.

chat.text: Hi, can I come in for a trim today?
I can do late morning or after lunch.

episodes.title: First Haircut
episodes.text: You seat your customer and ask what she wants. You look at her hair type and facial features. You pick up your scissors and clippers and start to cut, trim and shape.

trial.title: Order the haircut steps
items: Cut, trim and shape the hair
Listen to the customer's instructions
Look at hair type and facial features
Pick up clippers, scissors, trimmers and razors
trial.explain: You listen first, then check hair, then pick tools, then cut.

episodes.title: Tint Not Sitting Right
episodes.text: You brush tint onto a customer's hair and check the color. One section looks patchy and darker than she asked for. She watches you in the mirror and waits.

choice.prompt: The tint looks uneven while you still have time to fix it. What do you do?

options.label: Pause and blend more tint through the patchy section
options.outcome: You brush more tint through the light and dark spots. You recheck the color before rinsing.

options.label: Rinse now and offer to re-tint the patchy part
options.outcome: You rinse the tint out and show her the uneven part. You mix fresh tint and apply it just there.

episodes.title: Bleaching Carefully
episodes.text: You sit your next customer down for bleach. You brush it on section by section with the applicator. You watch it lift and rinse it out when ready.

episodes.title: Updating Customer Cards
episodes.text: You sit down with the customer information records. You write down the cuts and colors you did today. You file the cards so they are ready for next time.

episodes.title: Morning Calibration Checks
episodes.text: You arrive in the shop and pull the manufacturer's manual for the day's list. You set an infusion pump on the bench and connect your measuring device. You run the test and adjust the calibration until it reads true.

episodes.title: Cleaning Filters Again
episodes.text: You work through the same preventive maintenance carts as yesterday. You wipe housings, clean filters, and lubricate moving parts. You adjust the same knobs and check the same cords. Same again tomorrow.

episodes.title: Nurse Finds Fault
episodes.text: You walk up to the unit where a nurse is waiting by a monitor that keeps alarming.

choice.prompt: The nurse needs the monitor soon and you have two other calls waiting. What do you do first?

options.label: Run a quick test at the bedside now
options.outcome: You run the basic test and find a loose cable. You reseat it and the reading holds.

options.label: Take it to the shop for full troubleshooting
options.outcome: You tag it out and wheel in a spare. You test it fully on the bench later.

chat.text: It keeps dropping the reading, can you look now?
We need it for the next patient.

episodes.title: Pump Fails Test
episodes.text: You are testing a pump after lunch when it fails and will not start. You check the manual and your test instrument points to a dead motor. A nurse is waiting to use the pump.

choice.prompt: The pump is dead and needed on the floor. How do you handle it?

options.label: Pull it from service and give a spare
options.outcome: You tag the failed pump and bring a tested spare upstairs. You take the failed one back to the bench.

options.label: Try a quick fix at the bedside
options.outcome: You check power and connections with your meter. It still will not run, so you pull it from service.

options.label: Ask your supervisor what to prioritize
options.outcome: Your supervisor tells you to swap in a spare first. You do the swap, then return to troubleshoot.

episodes.title: Opening The Housing
episodes.text: You bring the failed pump to the bench and unplug it. You open the housing with hand tools and lift out the bad motor. You fit the replacement motor and close it back up.

trial.title: Fix the failed pump
items: Replace the bad motor with a good one
Remove the bad motor from the pump
Test the pump after the repair
Disassemble the pump housing
trial.explain: You open it first, then remove and replace the bad part before testing.

episodes.title: Logging Today's Work
episodes.text: You sit down at the computer with your notes from the day. You enter the cleaning, tests, and the motor you replaced. You mark what still needs an update and close the log.

episodes.title: The core work
episodes.text: You start the main work of a Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA) — the core of the job, done properly, start to finish. No audience and no shortcut: this is the thing everything else in the day supports. This is the work the whole job is built around.

episodes.title: People time
episodes.text: People need things from you — questions, help, decisions. You deal with them one at a time, the way this job always does. Real people, real reactions — this is the human side of the job, as it actually feels.

choice.prompt: Someone you're working with asks you to take on one more thing — extra work, on top of everything already in front of you today.

options.label: Say yes and fit it in
options.outcome: You fit it in. The day runs longer, the work gets done properly — and the person who asked remembers that you said yes.

options.label: Say no, politely
options.outcome: You say no, and you say why. A short, slightly awkward moment — then the rest of your day stays yours.

options.label: Offer a smaller version
options.outcome: You offer the part you can actually do, and by when. Most days that's accepted — saying yes to everything is how this job burns people out.

episodes.title: Hands on
episodes.text: Tools-and-systems time: you work the equipment and the screens of the trade until the thing in front of you does what it should. Skilled, hands-on work — the part where being good at it shows.

trial.title: The check-in
trial.says: Hey — how's that thing coming along that you were working on?
options: It's on track. I'll flag it straight away if I need help or it slips.
Fine.
Honestly? Don't ask. It's a disaster.
trial.explain: The professional reply says where things stand and what happens next — short, honest, no drama.

episodes.title: The routine block
episodes.text: The same block as yesterday: the repeating tasks that never make the brochure. You do them again, carefully, because skipping them is exactly how mistakes happen. The same again tomorrow. This block repeats more than any other part of the job.

episodes.title: It goes wrong
episodes.text: Something goes wrong — it always does, some days. A problem lands on you that was in nobody's plan, and sorting it out is now your job. Unplanned and unavoidable — how the job feels when it pushes back.

episodes.title: The paperwork
episodes.text: End of day: notes, records, the write-up of everything you did. The work isn't finished until it's written down. Nobody's favourite part. It still has to be done, every day.

episodes.title: Checking Morning Weather
episodes.text: You arrive at the wheelhouse before sunrise. You spread the chart out and pull up the weather report. You check the tide table and the depth finder beside you.

trial.title: Plan the morning movement
items: Direct the ship's movement
Check the navigation equipment
Look over the chart for depths
Read the morning weather report
trial.explain: You check weather and charts and equipment before you direct any movement.

episodes.title: Setting Course and Speed
episodes.text: You stand at the helm as the wind picks up. You set the course wide of the shallow bar and slow for the cross-current. You hold that speed past the buoys.

episodes.title: Holding the Helm
episodes.text: You steer on the same straight channel you steered yesterday. You watch the radar and keep the speed steady. Same water tomorrow.

episodes.title: Bringing Her In
episodes.text: You take the conn as docking master near the berth. The deckhand calls down from the bow.

choice.prompt: The wind is pushing the bow off as you near the berth. What do you do?

options.label: Ease in slow and angle into the wind
options.outcome: You come in slow against the wind and set her softly against the berth.

options.label: Hold position and wait for the gust to pass
options.outcome: You hold offshore for a few minutes, then bring her in when the wind eases.

chat.text: Captain, wind is pushing the bow off. Line is ready port side.
Berth is tight on starboard. What do you want?

episodes.title: Stopping Unsafe Move
episodes.text: You see another small boat cutting close across your bow in shallow water. You sound the signal and hold your position. You keep your ship clear of the hazard.

choice.prompt: The other boat keeps coming into unsafe water near you. What do you do?

options.label: Stop your ship and hold steady
options.outcome: You stop and hold. The other boat passes clear and you get underway again.

options.label: Radio a warning and change speed
options.outcome: You call on the radio and slow down. The other boat turns away from the shallows.

options.label: Alter course to deeper water
options.outcome: You turn toward deeper water. You keep separation until the area is clear.

episodes.title: Following Lights Home
episodes.text: You steer by the buoys and the lighthouse as the light fades. You check the radar and the depth finder. You bring the vessel steady through the channel.

episodes.title: First Engine Starts
episodes.text: You arrive and walk down the line of motorboats. You start the first motor and stand back to watch it run. You listen for misfiring and watch for smoke.

trial.title: Watch The Run
trial.scenario: You start a motor and monitor it. It shakes hard with excessive vibration and puffs light smoke, then you hear uneven misfiring.
options: Shut it down and flag the excessive vibration first
Ignore the shake and wipe the seats
Paint the hull
trial.explain: Excessive vibration is a direct sign of malfunction you monitor for on start-up.

episodes.title: Oil and Filters
episodes.text: You drain the oil and swap the filters on the next motorboat. You refill it and wipe up. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Fixing Power Tilt
episodes.text: You sit beside the stern and work on a stiff power tilt. You free it up and test it up and down. You check the bilge pump beside it while you are there.

episodes.title: Mounting A Motor
episodes.text: You and a colleague lift a motor onto the back of a boat.

choice.prompt: The motor sits crooked on the mount. Do you bolt it or reset it?

options.label: Reset it now
options.outcome: You lift again and set it straight before you tighten the bolts. It takes ten more minutes.

options.label: Bolt it as is
options.outcome: You tighten it crooked. The boat will pull sideways on the test run and you will have to remount it.

chat.text: Ready? Lift on three.
It looks a little left to me. Shift it right?

episodes.title: Smoke On Test
episodes.text: You operate the boat out on the waterway at slow speed. You push up faster and thick smoke rolls out with a rough shudder.

choice.prompt: Smoke and vibration rise fast. What do you do?

options.label: Throttle down and head back
options.outcome: You ease off and idle back to the dock. You note smoke and vibration for the repair bench.

options.label: Hold speed to see more
options.outcome: You stay at speed a minute longer. The shaking gets worse and the motor cuts out.

options.label: Shut off and drift
options.outcome: You kill the motor and drift clear. You call for a tow back to the dock.

episodes.title: Writing The Day
episodes.text: You sit down with your forms at the bench. You write down each inspection and test result from today. You list the work you did and the work still to be done.

episodes.title: First Start Up
episodes.text: You arrive at the yard and step down into the hull. You turn the key and start the motor cold. You watch and listen for smoke, shaking, or misfiring.

choice.prompt: The motor starts but shakes hard and misfires. What do you do?

options.label: Shut it down now
options.outcome: You cut the key. The shaking stops and you note a likely misfire to check later.

options.label: Let it run a minute
options.outcome: You stay by the key and watch. The shake stays bad, so you shut it down.

episodes.title: Fixing Bilge Pump
episodes.text: You kneel by the bilge pump with your tools out. You open it up and test the connections. You find the pump will not move water at all.

trial.title: What needs fixing first
trial.scenario: You repair the bilge pump. You check the power tilt and power take-off and they move fine. The bilge pump stays dead and water sits in the bilge.
options: The dead bilge pump
The working power tilt
The working power take-off
trial.explain: The bilge pump is the one that is not working.

episodes.title: Oil and Filters
episodes.text: You drain the old oil and swap the filters on the next motorboat. It is the same job as yesterday. It will be the same job tomorrow.

episodes.title: Hanging The Motor
episodes.text: You and a coworker lift the motor to the transom.

chat.text: Ready to set it down?
Hold left, bolts are lining up.
Good. Tighten them down now.

episodes.title: Smoke On Water
episodes.text: You take the boat out to run it slow, then fast.

choice.prompt: Blue smoke trails the motor and it vibrates at speed. What do you do?

options.label: Throttle down and head in
options.outcome: You slow down and idle back to the dock. You shut it off for inspection.

options.label: Push faster to test it
options.outcome: You push up for a few seconds. The smoke thickens, so you back off and turn around.

options.label: Stop dead in the channel
options.outcome: You cut power and drift. You restart at idle and limp back in.

chat.text: See that smoke behind you?
Ease off and bring her back in.

episodes.title: Writing The Day
episodes.text: You sit at the bench with your notes. You write down test results and what you fixed. You list the smoke issue and the work still to do.
